progress: tactics + aggressions + wars written; pacts/defense/territories, events, civil actions still to write. Per-card copy counts are derived, not sourced -- see 'uncertain' fields.

militaryDeckTotalsPerAge.source: BGG thread 1454794 (box states 150 military + 179 civil cards; per-age counts 10/45/50/45 confirmed by physical count)

trimmingRules.2p: Remove all pact cards from the military decks before play (Age I has 2 pacts, Ages II and III have 4 each). Pacts are used only in 3- and 4-player games. (Civil decks: remove the 6 cards marked 3+ and the 3 cards marked 4 from each of the Age I/II/III civil decks.)
trimmingRules.3p: No military-deck cards are removed. (Civil decks: remove the 3 cards marked 4 from each of the Age I/II/III civil decks.)
trimmingRules.source: 1j1ju_rulebook.pdf (Full Game setup, p.22) + cge_code_of_laws.pdf (setup): military cards carry no 3+/4 corner marks; the only player-count trimming of military decks is the removal of all pacts in 2-player games.

metadata.ageAEventSeeding: Shuffle the Age A military deck (10 event cards); place the top (players+2) cards face down as the current events deck (2p:4, 3p:5, 4p:6). Return the rest to the box unseen. No one ever draws Age A military cards.
metadata.tacticsRules2015: Playing a tactic from hand costs 1 military action (Action Phase). After you replenish the card row at the start of your next turn (before your Politics Phase) the card moves to the common tactics area, where any player may copy it for 2 military actions. Age II/III tactics show a second, lesser strength used for outdated armies (any unit in the set 2+ levels lower than the tactic's age).
metadata.cardTextSource: Exact 2015 card texts reconstructed from the official digital-edition localization strings (MilitaryCards_card_texts / MilitaryCards_card_names, Russian localization repo yashcherU/Through-the-Ages_ru, which mirrors the shipped English strings 1:1), cross-checked against namu_military.txt, faq_v15.pdf and throughtheages.fandom.com. The digital edition implements the 2015 base rules exactly; expansion-only keys were excluded.
metadata.aggressionRules: Played as a political action against one opponent. Attacker pays the card's military action cost and reveals the card. The defender may add defense: military bonus cards (defense value in the upper half) plus any number of military cards discarded face down for +1 each; the total number of bonus cards played + cards discarded may not exceed the defender's military action total (2015 change: no unit sacrifice). Attacker strength > defender strength + defense bonus => the card's effect applies; otherwise the aggression fails and the card is discarded with no effect.
metadata.warRules: Declared as a political action; resolved at the start of the declarer's next turn, before the Politics Phase. No defense bonuses and no sacrifices at resolution (2015 change). Either side can be the victor: the victor is whoever has the strictly higher strength rating at resolution; the difference is the strength advantage fed into the card's formula. Equal strength = no effect, card discarded. Spoils are capped by what the loser actually has. If the target resigns, the declarer scores 7 culture.
